errors.text: The proposed material and specimen state do not reconstruct the target: the target is a periodic single-crystal equiatomic FeNiCrMn atomistic model, whereas the hypothesis concerns generic micron-grained quaternary alloys and gives CoCrFeNi or Al-containing examples.
The strain-rate and temperature regimes differ fundamentally: 10^-4–10^3 s^-1 and 77–300 K are substituted for the molecular-dynamics conditions of 10^8–10^10 s^-1 and 10–600 K.
The asserted SFE threshold of greater than 40 mJ/m² and the associated strain-rate-insensitivity criterion are not supported by the cited evidence.

The hypothesis predicts possible FCC-to-HCP/BCC transformation or amorphization at high rates, while the target mechanism is Shockley-partial slip producing stacking-fault-associated HCP-like signatures without bulk phase transformation.
It omits the target's crystallographic orientation dependence, vacancy-assisted dislocation nucleation, and maximum yield strength along the <-111> direction.
